Could be a few things. func is what is normally called 'obj' right? You don't for instance pass func=obj$fn to tmbstan -- it needs the whole object. 

Does the code at https://github.com/kaskr/tmbstan#examples run? If yes, then it seems related to your specific model. I'd try tmbstan(func, chains=1, iter=200, init='last.best.par', control=list(max_treedepth=2)) and see if that runs. Also try it outside of Rstudio.

-Cole

Saang-Yoon Hyun <shy...@gmail.com>: Apr 22 08:21AM +0900

Hi.
One of the most likely possibilities might lie in an index problem. The
set of "TMB - R - R studio" in the Windows machine is too sensitive to
an error in indexing, I observe. What I mean with an "indexing" error is
a mismatch between your intending to point an element in an array and
the corresponding element. Whenever running into the mismatch problem,
the R studio is forced to terminate. This is very annoying, and thus a few
friends, who use TMB, recommend we should use Linux or Mac for TMB instead
of Windows. Anyhow returning back to my main point, please check whether,
in your loop (e.g., for, while, etc.) in your CPP file, your indices were
correct. Recall that the TMB index starts at zero (i.e., i =0, not i=1).
Your attachment does not show your CPP file, and thus I am not sure though
that my guess is right.
Saang-Yoon
